title: Fewest Fuel Stops
statement:
A car drives east along a straight road from position 0 to position target. It starts with startFuel litres and burns exactly one litre per unit of distance. The tank has no size limit.

Along the road are fuel stations: stations[i] = [position, litres], sorted by strictly increasing position, all between 0 and target. Stopping at a station puts all of its litres into the tank.

Return the fewest stops needed to reach target, or -1 if it cannot be reached. Arriving somewhere with exactly 0 litres left still counts as arriving.

examples.why: You must stop at 10 (the tank is empty there). That gets you to 30. Skip the small station at 20 and stop at 30: 30 + 30 = 60 ≥ 50.
The car runs dry at 10, before the only station.
The tank empties exactly at the target, which is enough. No stop needed.

hints: You do not have to decide at a station whether to stop there. What if you could decide later?
Drive as far as the fuel allows, remembering every station you passed. When you would run dry, which of those past stations would you have wanted to stop at?
Keep the litres of passed stations in a max-heap. Each time the car cannot reach the next point, pop the biggest and count a stop. If the heap is empty, return −1.

explain.intuition:
Pretend the car can refuel "retroactively". Drive until the fuel runs out, and keep every station you went past in a pocket. When you cannot reach the next station or the target, you know you need one more stop somewhere behind you, and the best choice is obviously the station with the most fuel. Picking it can only push you further than any other single stop.

A max-heap is the pocket: pushing a passed station and taking the largest are both O(log n). Each pop is one real stop. Since only the count of stops matters, not where they were, this greedy is exact.
steps: Set reach = startFuel, stops = 0, and an empty max-heap.
Walk the stations, then the target as a last point with 0 litres.
While reach is less than the point's position: if the heap is empty return −1; else add the heap's max to reach and increment stops.
Push the station's litres into the heap.
pitfalls: Stopping at every station you reach, or at the first one that would help. In example 1 the station at 20 is a wasted stop.
Taking the biggest station overall, including ones you have not reached. Only passed stations may be used.
Treating arriving with 0 litres as failure. Use reach < position, not ≤.

solutions.title: DP on number of stops
solutions.idea: best[t] is the farthest the car can get with exactly t stops among the stations seen so far. Each station can raise best[t + 1] from any best[t] that reaches it; update t downward so a station is used once.

solutions.title: Max-heap of passed stations
solutions.idea: Drive on; when the fuel runs short, retroactively stop at the biggest station already passed.

followups: The tank now has a capacity. Why does the greedy break, and what would you do instead?
Return which stations to stop at, not just how many.
